commands.name: approval-gate
commands.summary: Bind a relayed go before its effect: approval-gate consume ... | complete <request-id> <outcome>.
commands.help:
usage: herdsman approval-gate consume <go-file> <action> <target> <revision> <draft-file|->
       herdsman approval-gate complete <request-id> <outcome>

Binds a relayed go to one effect: consume checks the go and records the
request (CONSUME, DUPLICATE, RECONCILE or REFUSED lines); complete records
its outcome (COMPLETED). --json prints each line as an Event object.

settings: HERDSMAN_INBOX (the inbox folder) is required. HERDSMAN_PREFLIGHT
names the setup proof, <inbox>/setup.json, which must name this herdsman
binary with its checksum. HEALTH_AFTER (1 to 86400) and LOCK_WAIT (1 to 60) are
strict settings. Herdr is reached through HERDR_SOCKET_PATH.

exit codes:
  0  consumed or completed; act once
  1  refused: the go does not bind this effect
  2  usage error, HERDSMAN_INBOX is not set, an invalid setting, or the
     inbox cannot be used
  3  a human must repeat the setup: the proof is missing, stale, or does
     not name this herdsman binary (an old proof that lists scripts too)
  4  a duplicate: the request already has an outcome
  5  reconcile: consumed without an outcome; inspect external state first

exitCodes.meaning: consumed or completed; act once
refused: the go does not bind this effect
usage error, HERDSMAN_INBOX is not set, an invalid setting, or the inbox cannot be used
a human must repeat the setup: the proof is missing, stale, or does not name this herdsman binary (an old proof that lists scripts too)
a duplicate: the request already has an outcome
reconcile: consumed without an outcome; inspect external state first

commands.name: commit
commands.summary: Commit a worktree with a Conventional Commits message.
commands.help:
usage: herdsman commit [--squash <target>] [--dry-run] [-m <message>] [--type <type>] [--scope <scope>] [--json]

Stages the current worktree by its [commit] stage policy and commits. The
message is written by the configured generator, from the staged diff, and must
be a Conventional Commits message. When no generator can answer, the command
writes a plain one from the branch and the file names and says so; an answer
that is still invalid after one retry stops the commit.

--squash folds every commit since the branch left <target> into this one.
--dry-run shows the request, which program gets it and its answer; nothing changes.

exit codes:
  0  committed, or the dry run printed
  1  nothing to commit, an invalid message, or git refused
  2  bad usage

exitCodes.meaning: committed, or the dry run printed
nothing to commit, an invalid message, or git refused
bad usage

commands.name: config
commands.summary: Read and change the configuration; install the shell integration.
commands.help:
usage: herdsman config get <key> [-c <path>]
       herdsman config set <key> <value> [-c <path>]
       herdsman config unset <key> [-c <path>]
       herdsman config show [--strict] [-c <path>]
       herdsman config export --format toml|yaml|json|bin [-c <path>]
       herdsman config update [-c <path>]
       herdsman config init [--format toml|yaml|json|bin] [-c <path>]
       herdsman config schema --format jsonschema|descriptor
       herdsman config approvals list
       herdsman config approvals clear [<project>]
       herdsman config shell install|uninstall [bash|zsh|fish] [--json]

Keys are dotted paths such as merge.strategy; a kebab-case spelling is the same
key. -c names a file; otherwise HERDSMAN_CONFIG, then the repository's parent
folder, then the repository root.

show prints the file in use and then one "key = value (source)" line each.
A warning goes to stderr; --strict makes it an error. An unknown key in the
policy or launch section always stops the command.

shell adds or removes the wrapper that lets herdsman go change the shell's
folder, with static completions. The shell defaults to $SHELL.

exit codes:
  0  done
  1  the configuration is invalid, or the file cannot be read or written
  2  usage error

exitCodes.meaning: done
the configuration is invalid, or the file cannot be read or written
usage error

commands.name: delete
commands.summary: Remove a route, once a verified snapshot makes that undoable.
commands.help:
usage: herdsman delete <route> [--force] [--keep-folder] [--keep-worktrees] [--grace <seconds>] [-y] [--dry-run]

Refuses while an agent of the route runs, unless --force, which stops the route
first. Takes a snapshot of the route folder and private inbox through the
recovery pipeline, and removes nothing unless that snapshot verifies and covers
every path it removes. The result names the operation to give "herdsman undo".
--keep-folder leaves the route folder in place; --keep-worktrees leaves the
route's tasks and their worktrees alone.

commands.help:
usage: herdsman diff [<task>] [--working|--committed|--remote] [--json] [-- <git diff args>]

Prints git's diff for a worktree, the current one when no task is named. With
no mode it is everything since the branch left the default branch, whether
committed, in the index, edited or new. Reading it stages nothing.

  --working    staged, unstaged and untracked changes against the last commit
  --committed  commits since the branch left the default branch
  --remote     commits the upstream does not have yet

exit codes:
  0  printed
  1  no such worktree, git refused, or --exit-code found differences
  2  bad usage

commands.name: each
commands.summary: Run a command in every worktree.
commands.help:
usage: herdsman each [--json] -- <command> [<arg>...]

Runs a command in each worktree of the repository in turn; a failure in one
does not stop the rest. The command is run as given, without a shell; use
sh -c '...' for one. It sees HERDSMAN_TASK, HERDSMAN_BRANCH and
HERDSMAN_WORKTREE_PATH, and reads nothing from standard input.

The command's output goes to standard output. The heading before each run and
the summary go to standard error, so the output can be piped. With --json the
command's output moves to standard error too and standard output holds only the
results.

exit codes:
  0  the command succeeded everywhere
  1  it failed somewhere, or the worktrees could not be listed
  2  bad usage

exitCodes.meaning: the command succeeded everywhere
it failed somewhere, or the worktrees could not be listed
bad usage

commands.name: eval
commands.summary: Report a suite's runs with intervals and an A/A control (experimental).
commands.help:
usage: herdsman eval --experimental-eval <suite folder> [--json] [--findings <route folder>]... [--rank]
       herdsman eval --experimental-eval finding add <route folder> --reviewer <name> --severity <level>
                     --title <text> [--id <id>] [--task <task>] [--head <commit>] [--file <path>] [--line <n>]
       herdsman eval --experimental-eval finding outcome <route folder> <id> dismissed|accepted|fixed

Experimental: the flag is required and the format can change between minor
releases. Reports a suite's recorded runs (runs.jsonl in the suite folder) per
arm: counts, and 95% confidence intervals of pass rate, duration and cost, with
an A/A control of two groups of the same arm. Every arm needs its own control;
a suite with an arm that has none is refused. Only ranges are reported, never a single value.

Each --findings route adds its reviewer findings, counted by outcome. --rank
never ranks: it reports why not, and exits 3.

exit codes:
  0  reported or recorded
  1  a file could not be read or written, or the suite has no A/A control
  2  bad usage, or the experimental flag is missing
  3  a ranking was asked for and refused

exitCodes.meaning: reported or recorded
a file could not be read or written, or the suite has no A/A control
bad usage, or the experimental flag is missing
a ranking was asked for and refused

commands.name: mcp
commands.summary: Serve the daemon's services as MCP tools over stdio.
commands.help:
usage: herdsman mcp [--socket <path>] [--config <file>] [--deny <tool>]...

Serves the daemon's services as MCP tools on stdin and stdout.

  --socket  the daemon's socket (default: found as other commands find it)
  --config  the configuration file (default: found as other commands find it)
  --deny    refuse a tool: a name, a name pattern, or service/method (repeatable)

The [policy] deny list of the configuration refuses tools in the same three
forms, and --deny adds to it. The configuration is read on every call; while it
cannot be read, every tool is refused.

Calls that act for a party identify it by HERDR_PANE_ID and HERDSMAN_NAME.

  1  serving failed
  2  bad usage

commands.name: pause
commands.summary: Interrupt a route's agents and hold its channel; every pane stays open.
commands.help:
usage: herdsman pause <route> [--teardown] [-y] [--dry-run]

Sends each agent the interrupt key, stops the checkpointer's prompts and holds
the message channel. The interrupt is best effort: an agent acts on it at its
next turn boundary. <route> is a route name, a route folder, or @ for the route
of the current folder. --teardown also stops the route's task processes.

commands.name: plugin
commands.summary: Manage plugins (experimental).
commands.help:
usage: herdsman plugin --experimental-plugins <verb> [args] [--json]

  list                   the plugins found, usable or not
  describe <name>        a plugin's manifest
  install <path|name>    copy an executable into the plugin folder and ask for approval
  remove <name>          delete an installed plugin and its approval
  verify <name>          run the conformance checks for its extension points
  run <name>             start it in the foreground, for development

Plugins are experimental, so every use needs --experimental-plugins. A plugin
runs only after a person approves its exact checksum, at a terminal.

commands.name: resume
commands.summary: Continue a paused route, or restart a stopped one from its record.
commands.help:
usage: herdsman resume <route> [-p <text>] [-y] [--dry-run]

On a paused route, lifts the channel hold, starts the checkpointer again and

service panes again with the commands recorded by up; the launch prelude does
not run again, and the pair is attested and approved again.

commands.name: run-check
commands.summary: Run one heavy check at a time on this machine, behind a load gate (--publish <hours>: the load reading).
commands.help:
usage: herdsman run-check <command> [args]
       herdsman run-check --publish <hours>

Runs one heavy check at a time on this machine, under a shared lock, behind
a load gate, at a lower priority. --publish writes the machine's load
reading every HERDSMAN_PUBLISH_EVERY for <hours> (or
HERDSMAN_PUBLISH_SECONDS), at most a day.

settings: HERDSMAN_LOCK, HERDSMAN_READING, HERDSMAN_LOCK_WAIT (5400),
HERDSMAN_GATE_WAIT (600), HERDSMAN_GATE_POLL (15), HERDSMAN_MIN_FREE (10),
HERDSMAN_NICE (10), HERDSMAN_LOAD_LIMIT (the core count), HERDSMAN_PROBES,
HERDSMAN_PUBLISH_EVERY (15), HERDSMAN_PUBLISH_SECONDS. Durations are seconds
or a number with s, m, h or d.

exit codes:
  N   the check's own exit code
  2   an invalid setting or hour count; nothing ran
  64  usage error
  69  the lock file cannot be opened or locked
  70  the start marker cannot be written
  73  the publisher cannot write its reading (--publish)
  75  the load gate gave up, or no lock came within HERDSMAN_LOCK_WAIT
  126 the command cannot be started
  127 the command was not found

commands.name: stop
commands.summary: End a route's sessions and service panes; the work stays on disk.
commands.help:
usage: herdsman stop <route> [--grace <seconds>] [--teardown] [-y] [--dry-run]

Asks each agent for its report, waits up to --grace seconds (default 120), then
closes the agent and service panes and retires the pair. Worktrees, branches,
the route folder and the inbox stay. A stopped route can be resumed.

commands.name: trace
commands.summary: Show or export one route's spans as OpenTelemetry.
commands.help:
usage: herdsman trace <route folder> [--json | --otlp <endpoint>] [--hook-logs <folder>]...
       herdsman trace add <route folder> --kind <kind> --name <name> [--task <task>]
                          [--start <RFC 3339>] [--duration-ms <n>] [--exit <n>]
                          [--tokens <n>] [--cost-micros <n>]

Shows one route as spans: git commands, hooks, checks, reviews and agent
turns, each with its timing and whatever exit or usage was reported. --json
prints them; --otlp posts them to an OpenTelemetry collector over HTTP (plain
http only to this machine). Each --hook-logs folder adds every hook run in it,
since a hook result does not name its route. Secrets are kept out: git
arguments are redacted and hook command text is left out.

commands.summary: Start a route: workspace, private inbox, both coordinators, the pair and the first brief.
commands.help:
usage: herdsman up <route> -p <prompt> -a <command> -o <command> [-c <config>]
                   [--adjutant-kind <kind>] [--orchestrator-kind <kind>] [--no-adjutant]
                   [--pair auto|manual] [--web] [--no-attach] [--dry-run]
       herdsman up [<route>] --continue [--step <n>=done|rerun]...

-a and -o are the commands that launch each coordinator's harness, typed as you
would type them: "claude doctor && claude --model opus".
--dry-run prints the whole plan and starts nothing.
--web also starts the web app on the route.
--pair manual asks on the terminal before the pair is approved. Under the
restricted profile it is the default and auto is refused.
A second up on the same route picks up where the first stopped.

commands.name: update
commands.summary: Install the latest signed release over this binary.
commands.help:
usage: herdsman update [--check] [--version <version>] [--allow-downgrade]

Installs the latest release over this binary. The release's checksum list must
carry a signature from a key this binary trusts, and the archive must match
that list, before anything is replaced; the new binary must also run and report
its version. A binary installed by a package manager is left to that manager.

  --check            Say whether a newer release exists; change nothing.
  --version <v>      Install this version instead of the latest.
  --allow-downgrade  Allow a version older than this binary.

exit codes:
  0  the binary is current, was updated, or --check answered
  1  the release was refused or could not be fetched; the binary is unchanged
  2  usage error
